_comment: M3 workplace events (Kimi C, 2026-11-21). Gated by the shared v3 condition path: every event requires an ACTIVE named-career assignment (active_assignment); several narrow to a ladder via role_ids. Actor-only, all options free, outcome lines carry their context.

events.title: The Weekend Ask
events.text: My manager has asked if I will come in this Saturday to help catch up on the backlog.

choices.label: Go in and help
choices.outcome_text: I gave up my Saturday for the team and the backlog shrank; the extra cash in my pocket softened the sting.

choices.label: Protect the weekend
choices.outcome_text: I told my manager I had plans and kept my weekend; the backlog was still waiting on Monday, but so was my sanity.

events.title: Show Them the Ropes
events.text: A nervous new starter has been assigned to shadow me for the week, and they are watching everything I do.

choices.label: Teach them properly
choices.outcome_text: I slowed down and taught my shadow every trick I know; by Friday they were grinning instead of flinching.

choices.label: Let them figure it out
choices.outcome_text: I let the new starter sink or swim on their own; they survived, but I do not think they will thank me for it.

events.title: Something's Opening Up
events.text: Word around the workplace is that a senior position is about to be advertised, and a colleague thinks I should go for it.

choices.label: Start preparing now
choices.outcome_text: I began quietly preparing for the rumored promotion, polishing my record so I would be ready when it posted.

choices.label: Wait and see
choices.outcome_text: I decided not to chase the rumor of a promotion and just kept doing my job well; whatever opens, opens.

events.title: The Favour
events.text: A colleague has begged me to swap shifts next week because of a family thing they cannot miss.

choices.label: Swap shifts
choices.outcome_text: I swapped shifts so my colleague could make their family thing; my week got awkward but my conscience got lighter.

choices.label: Sorry, I can't
choices.outcome_text: I told my colleague I could not swap shifts this time, and I carried a small guilty feeling to my next break.

events.title: The Missing Sandwich
events.text: Someone keeps taking food from the staff fridge, and today it was my carefully packed lunch.

choices.label: Leave a passive-aggressive note
choices.outcome_text: I taped a stern note to the staff fridge about my stolen lunch; whether it worked, my dignity felt restored.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.outcome_text: I let the lunch thief keep their secrets and bought something hot instead; some battles are not worth the appetite.

events.title: Not Now, Alarm
events.text: A fire drill has emptied the whole building in the middle of my most productive hour.

choices.label: Enjoy the break outside
choices.outcome_text: I treated the fire drill as an unscheduled holiday and chatted in the carpark until the all-clear sounded.

choices.label: Stress about the deadline
choices.outcome_text: I spent the whole fire drill fretting about my deadline, and the work was no shorter when we filed back in.

events.title: The Unhappy Customer
events.text: A furious customer is demanding to speak to someone in charge, and that someone is currently me.

choices.label: Listen and fix it
choices.outcome_text: I listened to the furious customer without interrupting, fixed their problem, and watched their anger deflate.

choices.label: Hide behind policy
choices.outcome_text: I hid behind company policy with the angry customer; they left unsatisfied, and so did I, to be honest.

events.title: The Filing Mountain
events.text: A mix-up means three weeks of unfiled paperwork has landed on my desk at once.

choices.label: Tackle it head-on
choices.outcome_text: I rolled up my sleeves and worked through the whole filing mountain in one long afternoon; my desk has never looked so smug.

choices.label: Spread it over the week
choices.outcome_text: I quietly spread the paperwork avalanche across the whole week; slower, but my evenings stayed my own.

events.title: Mandatory Fun
events.text: The office party is tonight and someone has already mentioned karaoke twice.

choices.label: Go and own the karaoke
choices.outcome_text: I went to the office party and gave the karaoke my full, tuneless commitment; my colleagues will not forget it.

choices.label: Make an excuse
choices.outcome_text: I invented a vague excuse and skipped the office party, trading karaoke regret for a quiet evening at home.

events.title: The Coffee Rota Wars
events.text: Someone has 'forgotten' the tea-round rota three days running, and the kitchen tension is boiling.

choices.label: Just make the round
choices.outcome_text: I gave up on the rota and made the tea round myself; peace returned to the kitchen, sweetened with sugar.

choices.label: Call out the shirker
choices.outcome_text: I confronted the colleague dodging the tea rota; the kitchen is fair again, if a little frosty toward me now.

events.title: Inspector on Site
events.text: A safety inspector has just walked onto the site and is heading straight for the area I was working in yesterday.

choices.label: Walk them through it proudly
choices.outcome_text: I walked the safety inspector through my work area with nothing to hide, and the pass mark felt like a medal.

choices.label: Quietly fix last week's corner-cutting
choices.outcome_text: I quietly tidied up the shortcuts I had taken before the inspector reached them; lesson learned, heart hammering.

events.title: The Rerun
events.text: I have just realised I ran the wrong cable through half of today's job and nobody has noticed yet.

choices.label: Admit it and redo it
choices.outcome_text: I owned up to the wrong cable and redid the whole run; it cost me the afternoon but bought me a clear conscience.

choices.label: Hope nobody checks
choices.outcome_text: I said nothing about the wrong cable and hoped it would never matter; the worry followed me home anyway.

events.title: Old Faithful Gives Up
events.text: The ancient machine I rely on has made a noise like a dying whale and stopped dead mid-job.

choices.label: Try to coax it back to life
choices.outcome_text: I opened up the dying machine and coaxed it back to life with patience and one well-placed thump; the job survived.

choices.label: Report it and wait
choices.outcome_text: I reported the dead machine and waited out the delay; sometimes the bravest move is admitting the whale won.

events.title: Flying Solo
events.text: For the first time, the boss has sent me to a job entirely on my own.

choices.label: Show them what I can do
choices.outcome_text: I flew solo on my first lone job and finished clean; the quiet pride of it stayed with me all week.

choices.label: Call for advice twice
choices.outcome_text: I handled my first solo job with two cautious calls to the boss; slow and correct beats fast and wrong.

events.title: Trust Falls and Other Horrors
events.text: Head office has organised a compulsory team-building day involving exercises I can only describe as crimes against dignity.

choices.label: Throw yourself in
choices.outcome_text: I threw myself into the team-building day with alarming enthusiasm; my colleagues found it either inspiring or unsettling.

choices.label: Endure it with minimum effort
choices.outcome_text: I endured the team-building exercises with the bare minimum of movement and eye contact; dignity mostly intact.

events.title: The Lean Season
events.text: Management has announced budget cuts, and everyone is quietly wondering what gets trimmed first.

choices.label: Volunteer improvement ideas
choices.outcome_text: I met the budget cuts with a list of practical savings; management actually adopted two of my ideas.

choices.label: Keep your head down
choices.outcome_text: I kept my head well below the parapet during the budget cuts and quietly made myself harder to trim.

events.title: Indoor Weather
events.text: A storm has opened a leak directly above my desk and my paperwork is in the splash zone.

choices.label: Mount a bucket defence
choices.outcome_text: I organised a bucket brigade over my desk and saved the paperwork; the indoor rain became an office legend.

choices.label: Move everything immediately
choices.outcome_text: I evacuated my desk from the leak in one frantic trip and worked from a windowsill for the rest of the day.

events.title: Two Places at Once
events.text: A scheduling error has double-booked me for two different appointments at the same time.

choices.label: Reprioritise and rebook
choices.outcome_text: I untangled the double-booking by priority, rebooked the less urgent visit, and nobody was left waiting on me.

choices.label: Sprint between both
choices.outcome_text: I tried to honour both double-booked appointments by sprinting between them; I made it, barely, and ached after.

events.title: The Note That Made the Week
events.text: Someone I helped at work has sent a handwritten thank-you note to my supervisor, and it has been pinned to the noticeboard.

choices.label: Savour it quietly
choices.outcome_text: I read the thank-you note on the noticeboard twice and floated through the rest of my shift; this is why I do the work.

choices.label: Frame it at home
choices.outcome_text: I photocopied the kind note before pinning it back, and framed my copy at home for the days the work feels heavy.

events.title: Access Denied
events.text: My access badge has demagnetised and the security desk is enjoying this far too much.

choices.label: Charm the security desk
choices.outcome_text: I charmed the security desk until they waved me through the dead badge and issued a temporary pass with a smile.

choices.label: Do the paperwork properly
choices.outcome_text: I queued for the proper replacement badge and filled in the form; dull, correct, and permanently fixed.

events.title: The Old Guard Bows Out
events.text: The boss everyone respected has announced their retirement, and the whole workplace is quietly measuring what changes next.

choices.label: Give a heartfelt speech
choices.outcome_text: I gave the retiring boss a heartfelt send-off speech; several people cried and the boss shook my hand twice.

choices.label: Watch from the back
choices.outcome_text: I watched the retirement send-off from the back row, waving once when the old boss scanned the room for familiar faces.

events.title: The Good Pens
events.text: I have discovered who has been hoarding all the good pens in the stationery cupboard, and it is exactly who everyone suspected.

choices.label: Negotiate a fair share
choices.outcome_text: I negotiated a pen treaty with the stationery hoarder; the good pens now circulate like a small, smooth economy.

choices.label: Report the hoard
choices.outcome_text: I reported the stationery hoard to management; the pens returned, but the kitchen has been very quiet near me since.

events.title: Eight Flights of Honesty
events.text: The lift is out of order again and my next appointment is on the top floor.

choices.label: Take the stairs
choices.outcome_text: I climbed the eight flights to the top-floor appointment and arrived pink, punctual, and weirdly proud of my legs.

choices.label: Wait for the repair
choices.outcome_text: I waited out the broken lift and rescheduled the top-floor visit; the stairs will still be there tomorrow, unfortunately.

events.title: Surprise Audit
events.text: A surprise audit team has arrived to inspect our records and facilities, unannounced.

choices.label: Assist the auditors fully
choices.outcome_text: I dropped everything to assist the surprise audit team, and our facility passed with only minor notes.

choices.label: Stay out of their way
choices.outcome_text: I kept a respectful distance from the surprise auditors and let my records speak for themselves; they did, mostly.

events.title: The New Uniform
events.text: Head office has issued a new uniform policy that everyone agrees makes us look like lost referees.

choices.label: Wear it with pride
choices.outcome_text: I wore the ridiculous new uniform with full commitment; if I looked like a lost referee, I was the proudest one on the field.

choices.label: Join the muttered protest
choices.outcome_text: I joined the quiet mutiny against the new uniform policy; the shirt stays in the drawer until someone enforces it.

events.title: Sent Home Early
events.text: A wild storm has knocked the power out and management is deciding whether to send everyone home.

choices.label: Pack up and hope
choices.outcome_text: The storm sent us all home early; I celebrated the unexpected holiday with soup and the smug comfort of my own couch.

choices.label: Offer to stay and secure things
choices.outcome_text: I stayed late through the storm to secure the worksite; soaked shoes, but the boss noticed who stayed.

events.title: Back to Class
events.text: My employer is offering a short refresher workshop that would sharpen exactly the skills I use daily.

choices.label: Attend the workshop
choices.outcome_text: I attended the employer's refresher workshop and came back with new tricks that made my daily work noticeably smoother.

choices.label: Skip it, I'm busy
choices.outcome_text: I skipped the refresher workshop to keep up with the day job; efficient now, maybe costlier later.
